name: Duskrow Moto Jacket
description:
A motorcycle jacket built for the Shelf and lower Tier 2, where looking hard is sometimes the only armor you've got. The Duskrow is made from bonded synth-hide — not leather, not pretending to be — in a flat, worn-in black with faint horizontal ribbing across the shoulders and forearms. The cut is boxy enough to move in, with an asymmetric zip closure, two chest pockets with snap flaps, and a wide lapel collar that can be turned up against the wind off the lake. Pre-scuffed at the elbows. That's not a flaw. That's the design.

People who wear the Duskrow aren't trying to impress anyone at a Tier 3 wine bar. They're couriers, fixers, gig workers who ride secondhand mopeds through the Shelf's cracked-asphalt corridors. The jacket shows up in markets, in dive bars, in the back of dispatch vans. It holds its shape after a fall. It doesn't crack in the cold. It's the kind of jacket you hand down.
what_it_says: You don't have much, but you've got a code — and you've been around long enough that the jacket shows it.
story_hooks: A jacket matching this description was worn by the only witness to a Shelf-level corporate dump — now someone is buying up every Duskrow in that colorway from secondhand stalls, looking for the right one.
The original Duskrow factory in the lower Shelf burned down six years ago; what's sold now is knockoffs of knockoffs, but an original pre-fire jacket has cult status among collectors.
A courier dies wearing one and the jacket ends up in a lost-and-found bin — the inside lining has a name and a locker number stitched into it.
